title: Quarterly Commitment Lattice: Endpoint Tiering, Variant Hedging & Canary Windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a quarter-long commitment lattice that maps endpoint tiering decisions (tier-0 / tier-1 / experimental), model-variant hedging rules, and explicit canary windows for hosted endpoints and the public model catalog. Purpose: reduce surprise regressions at release boundaries, limit blast radius for model rotations, and provide clear rollback/fallback policies for customers and Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Published lattice doc describing tier definitions, commit thresholds, and rollback triggers
Canary window scheduling UI wireframes and API contract reviewed by Console and Runtime teams
Automated smoke test suite for canaries added to CI with pass/fail thresholds
Fallback policy mapping that ties each hosted endpoint to a fallback variant and region preference
Operational runbook with SLA impact matrix and customer comms templates ready
decisions: Adopt a three-tier endpoint classification (Stable, Beta, Ephemeral) for this quarter to simplify commitments
Require 72-hour canary windows for Stable tier model rotations with progressive ramping (1% -> 10% -> 50%)
Mandate automated evaluation on the curated prompt set before canary start; if quality regression > 2% on key metrics, abort rollout
Use lightweight model-variant hedging: always keep the last known-good variant available as fallback for all Stable endpoints
tradeoffs: Longer canary windows increase time-to-commit but reduce customer-facing risk
Keeping fallbacks increases storage and capacity costs for hosted pools but prevents high-severity incidents
Stricter gating based on evals may block fast model improvements for experimental workloads
